---
title: "Conclusion"
---

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="65%"}
- Visualizations are often the most effective way to convey complex statistical results to both statistically savvy **and** non-statistically savvy audiences
  - Visualizations increase the audience for your work
  - Visualizations also help you understand your own data and results
- Be creative; data visualization gives you the chance to bring some art into the science of data analysis
  - Talks and research papers can (sometimes) be boring \[sad but true!\]
    - Visualizations offer a way to grab the attention of your audience
:::
::: {.column width="35%"}
![](images/art-and-science.png){fig-alt="A balance scale with a brain on one side and a heart on the other and a question mark in the middle."}
:::
::::

## Go forth and make pretty graphs

- The magical thing about data visualizations is that they are simultaneously:
  - Easier to understand than tables
  - And show a broader range of your data/findings
    - E.g., Predictions across the entire range of the data
    - E.g., The entire magnitude of a variable's effect
- So, go forth and visualize your data and models!
  - Using pretty graphs and clean plots, of course 😊

![](images/beautiful-clean-plots.jpeg){width=50% fig-alt="Meme of a woman singing with outstretched arms in a mountain meadow, captioned: Look at all these beautiful clean plots."}
